utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. May I call the case number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the case number is IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. My monitor as yet, at least, is -- I did press -- yeah, and I pressed it already. Oh, yes. It's coming now. Okay. Mr. Brdjanin, can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Good day. Yes, I can hear you in a language that I can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. And thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Appearance for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman with Milan Trbojevic and Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic and Natasha Ivanovic-Fauveau for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I notice, Mr. Zecevic, that your client is not present today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we have his consent to proceed in his absence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And may I take this first opportunity I have to congratulate you, Mr. Ackerman, and you, Mr. Zecevic, for your respective appointment as president -- first president and first vice-president of the newly formed Defence Attorneys Association.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's an honour which I'm sure you both deserve. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am informed that the representative of the FRY has just arrived. I suppose we can proceed with admitting him in the courtroom straight away. Any objection to that or anything you would like to raise before -- okay. Please, usher. I think we need two chairs. Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I see that you are prepared to address us. Could I kindly ask you to repeat your name again for the record, please, and your capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, distinguished member of the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may sit down, by the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, distinguished member of the court, my name is Slavoljub Caric, and I am the councillor of the Embassy of FRY, and I will present the explanation of guarantees of government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in the case of Mr. Talic for provisional release of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you --

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: -- the explanation in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you proceed, may I ask the gentleman who is sitting to your right to introduce himself and ask him also whether he will be addressing this Chamber. You may sit down. You may remain seated. [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, my name is Miodrag Panceski, I'm the first secretary of the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in The Hague. I'm here before you to help colleague Caric present the guarantees of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Allow me to inform you that in this case only my colleague Mr. Caric shall present -- shall address you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Caric, you may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] The Federal Republic -- the federal government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in the Momir Talic case, which is being conducted in front of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, under IT-99-36/1 suggests that the above-mentioned person be provisionally released in order to undergo medical treatment at the military academy -- at the Military Academy Hospital in Belgrade. And we undertake, if the Trial Chamber should render a decision according to which the accused Momir Talic may be allowed to defend himself while out free, we undertake to respect all the Trial Chamber's orders, and if necessary, to surrender Momir Talic to the International Criminal Tribunal at any time if so requested. This guarantee includes under A, the undertaking of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to take over Momir Talic from the Dutch authorities at the Schiphol airport at a time and a date to be determined by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please slow down, because you're going too fast for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Under B, we undertake, the Yugoslav authorities undertake to escort the accused during his journey to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Under C, the Yugoslav authorities undertake to escort the accused from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to the Schiphol airport and to hand him over to the Dutch authorities at a date and time to be determined by the Trial Chamber. The accused shall personally -- we shall personally take the accused from the Dutch authorities and escort him during his journey and surrender him to the Dutch authorities, and this shall be done by someone whom the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia shall appoint. Under E, we undertake, the Ministry of the Interior undertaking through the relevant secretary of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, we undertake to ensure that the accused shall report on a daily basis to the police station for a record of this to be compiled, and we undertake for monthly written reports to be submitted in which it will be confirmed that the accused has complied with these obligations, and the international criminal Tribunal shall immediately be informed should the accused fail to present himself. Under F, the Yugoslav authorities undertake to immediately arrest the accused should he attempt to flee or should he violate any of the conditions of provisional release and we undertake to inform the International Criminal Tribunal of this in order to make preparations for him to be surrendered to the Tribunal again. This guarantee is being given by the federal government for humanitarian reasons above all, taking into consideration the serious medical condition of the accused, Momir Talic, and the need for him to be provided with medical treatment in a specialist institution in the military medical institution -- in the Military Medical Academy in Belgrade. The federal government guarantees this on the basis of the authority invested in them on the basis of Article 36 of the law on cooperation with the International Criminal Tribunal for prosecuting persons responsible for serious violations of international humanitarian law committed in the territory of the former Yugoslavia in 1991. The President of the federal government, Dragisa Pesic, has signed the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Who would like to go first?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have one question: Sir, you said that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia would comply with any conditions that the Court might impose. Would that include conditions not listed here?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: These are undertakings that we are quite ready to fulfil. We have accepted this. So these are not conditions. At the moment I'm not in a position to add anything else. All I can do is provide the Trial Chamber with a photocopy of the text that I have just read out, that is to say, of the guarantee. I apologise because everything happened very rapidly, so I am -- I will be submitting a photocopy that is not very good. But tomorrow with regard to the Martic case, Mr. Savo Markovic, the federal Minister of Justice will be coming to the Tribunal and he will be in a position to provide you with more details with regard to any questions you might have. Allow me, Your Honours, to provide you with a photocopy of this guarantee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I ask you if this will be followed by the usual note verbale, whether it will be formalised, in other words, by -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. But can I just remind you of what you said to us when you first started. You said that "If the Trial Chamber should render a decision according to which the accused Momir Talic may be allowed to defend himself free, we undertake to respect all the Trial Chamber's orders," and you then said that the guarantee includes and listed a number of items. Now, all that I want to know, sir, from you, if you can assist, is does that mean that the federal government, if we read this literally, will respect orders made by this Trial Chamber which are -- which include aspects outside those listed?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: All I can say, Your Honours, is that we stand by the decision that was presented, that is to say, that all the duties -- all the obligations that are to be determined by this Trial Chamber, these decisions will be respected. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And let me explain one reason why I'm asking you this. Clearly if he's undergoing treatment or too ill, he cannot report daily to a police station, and therefore it would be helpful to know if in those circumstances if the Trial Chamber were to make an order that the police were to go to where he was to check, that would be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. Zecevic, whether you would like to pose any questions to the councillor?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We don't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman? Any submissions?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, yes, but I don't think they're -- they're not going to trouble this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. But when I said "any submissions," with the understanding, as we did last time, whether you want them to be here or whether we can ask them to go back to the embassy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I don't mind at all, Your Honours. I mean, clearly I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Last time we decided -- and actually, it proved to be quite useful -- to proceed with the debate in their presence, and at the end of the day we realised that we did the right thing because we could ask certain questions which they could then report back upon. And knowing that the minister is coming tomorrow, perhaps there may be some relevant matters that can be raised by either -- either side and they could be referred to should we have any further difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I'm perfectly content to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So unless you have other urgent matters to attend to, and if you would like to remain and assist for the rest of the debate, you're free to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: We can stay until the end of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So at this point I think we will entertain any final submissions that you may have and then adjourn for a decision, depending, of course, on the submissions that will be forthcoming. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the guarantee is phrased in the terms of "provisional release." But it's our submission it's clear that very properly the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia will comply with any conditions imposed by Your Honours. Your Honours, our application remains the same: We don't oppose, as it were, a transfer of Momir Talic so that he may receive medical treatment in Belgrade. We do oppose for the reasons I expressed any kind of transfer that would involve him being allowed to go to Banja Luka, and indeed our request -- I have instructions to tell Your Honours that our request is still that the transfer be under terms of detention. The only other thing I would say is this, that in the event of Your Honours' ruling in favour of provisional release, as opposed to what we submit would be the proper course, then the conditions should include one that he should not be allowed to go to Banja Luka and clearly a condition merely that he report to the police station is not likely to be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, that's -- I would imagine that given the circumstances attaching -- special, particular circumstances attaching to his medical condition and what is likely to -- what this medical condition is likely to be in the future, it doesn't make much sense concentrating on a provision like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, again I say what I said last time. Any prognosis at the moment is so wrapped in doubt that one has to look at the situation, which is he may, for example, go into remission. I mean, anything is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And so Your Honour has to look at all eventualities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Even miracles can happen. So -- Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence stays by its motion for provisional release under Rule 65 and as well as the amendment to the motion for provisional release which was filed two days before. It leaves the opportunity for this Trial Chamber to decide whether it would accept the submission made by the -- by our learned colleague from the Prosecutor's side concerning the Banja Luka. As far as we have already stated that we will accept any conditions imposed by this Trial Chamber as the Trial Chamber deems fit in accordance with the jurisprudence of this Tribunal. There is one other thing that I would like to state very clearly, that we very strongly oppose a request filed by the Prosecutor in its Prosecutor's response concerning the -- the application for a stay of decision if provisional release is granted to our client. We're strongly opposing that due to the factors that we already stated about the time and his medical condition. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we're obliged under the Rules to put that in, and it depends very much, of course, on the terms of the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. And as I understand you, if I read you well, is -- it's that while in the context of the document, your response, you did rule out outright the possibility of provisional release, now you are sort of -- still against it but presenting it in a different perspective. If it excludes Banja Luka, if it excludes this or that. You're still against provisional release.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry if I've mislead you. As I say, I have strict instructions that our application remains the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Any further submissions? Now the position is as follows: We need to have the communication of from the federal -- from the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia translated into English. And Madam Registrar, this must receive the -- must be done with the utmost urgency, if possible within the hour. Because although we can have the transcript -- although we can have the transcript, I would rather have a proper translation of it made by the office that does the translation, because a word here or a word there may make a difference and I want to make sure of the text that we could possibly rely upon if we hand down an order accepting or modifying the motion of General Talic. That's number one. Number two, of course you realise we need to sit down together, the three Judges, and discuss this last development; namely, the communication from the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. We will do that immediately after this sitting. And then there will be nothing left except to draft the decision and hand it down at the first opportunity. We promise you we will not sleep on it. We will -- we will give it our utmost attention. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt, but I would like to make another -- or actually inform the Trial Chamber that we have filed with the UNDU the personal guarantees and it's been signed by our client. And according to the procedure, it should have been filed with the Registry. I don't know. We don't have any information at this moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It has been filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think I can come -- I can come to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If was just wondering because we haven't received a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. It has been filed, Mr. Zecevic, and as well as the other document which you filed in --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- confidential. This is a document you're referring to which is the personal guarantees.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is right, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, it's almost superfluous to say that if we decide to grant some kind of release, be it under a detention regime or under a provisional release regime, it may go beyond these guarantees, and no such order will become operative unless there are the guarantees.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, as I take it, the guarantees which are being offered by the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia contain, as I see it, at least for the time being, a general umbrella clause which should prove to be extremely helpful. As regards General Talic, however, if we come to a conclusion to release him, there will be more than this that will be needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We understand that, Your Honour, and we are prepared -- our client is prepared to sign this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just ask, is it your intention to give a decision, as it were, in full verbally and then reduce it to writing today or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. It's -- Ms. Korner, the situation is too complicated and too delicate and we've come to the conclusion that we better hand down proper written judgement straight away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because there are more -- there are several aspects involved and we would rather select our words properly and make sure --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, then I think if -- if I may ask, if Your Honours rise, we could -- to discuss the progress, because it has -- on the understanding that one way or another General Talic is not going to be present at this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, let's -- you can take it that one way or another --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- he will not be present for two obvious reasons: If we release him, he is not going to be here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And there is always the problem of his consent.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay? Over which we will not have any control, because he will -- he will not be physically present anywhere nearby that we can control. But we can control it from a distance and we will have to depend on several others. That's number one. The second thing: If we don't give release, I think it would be very short-sighted on your part to anticipate him being present here. So you will still face the same problem, not just you but also us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, Your Honour, I don't think this aspect need trouble these two gentlemen any longer, so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would rather have them here, to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I can assure you this has got nothing to do with the federal government of Yugoslavia, but anyhow ... Your Honour, the first thing is this: Accepting that, there are two possibilities for whatever happens. The first is that the trial continues against General Talic in his absence. That requires, as it were, a general waiver from General Talic. I've had some conversation with Defence counsel, and I think I know what the answer is going to be, but I'd be grateful if perhaps they could deal with whether that is going to be given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You mean jointly with Brdjanin or separate?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I mean the trial goes on as a joint trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As a joint trial. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have already informed this Honourable Trial Chamber and our learned friends from the Prosecutor that our client has waived his right of presence for the witness which was in the course of the cross-examination and the other two witnesses. And what we suggested -- because we in all honesty do not -- do not see how it would be possible that -- that any accused would give a general waiver, because he has to specifically know what he's waiving his right from. So what we suggested was that each Thursday when we get the list of -- from the Prosecutor, we will inform them that day or perhaps on Friday morning about the waiver of our client for the next week. That is the best what we can do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Chamber, of course, reserves its position on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are making this very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think I need to draw Your Honours' attention to the problems with that. I say that I have instructions to continue against both, but it's a ruling for Your Honours to make. The second option - and can I say that this is the matter for Your Honours to make the ruling and I'm not going to say anything more on it - is that the trial against General Talic is severed from that of Mr. Brdjanin, and Your Honours will obviously make the ruling on that. In the event that Your Honours rule that it's the second option that happens, I -- I think it -- really the ball is in the Defence court to this extent. I would be asking for time, but the time that I would ask for, because it means a reconsideration of, if you like, the emphasis of the evidence and the sort of evidence, would be for no more than a week. There are two ways of achieving that. One is that we have next week off but we sit again, not to waste any further time, on the 30th of September, which at present is the week that Your Honours have arranged to take off. Failing that, I will try and arrange for the witness -- if not -- I'm not sure I can get him back for Monday -- but who was being cross-examined, to be back on Tuesday and at least use up next week and take the following week to reconsider the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 30th and -- 30th September, 1st October there's going to be a plenary session here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge's plenaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: On the 30th of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And 1st of October. 30th September and 1st October.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, in that case, unless there's an objection I think I'll make arrangements to see if I can get at least Mr. Filipovic back for next week. But that's why I say -- and we'll use the week of the 30th to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But let's hear, because also, I mean, I -- we are in the habit here of respecting what may have been previous arrangements if commitments have arisen out of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But we were always sitting next week, Your Honour. We were always sitting next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Okay. That, I understand. I would not have expected anyone to make any different commitments as far as next week is concerned. But as far as the -- the following week is concerned, I have an impression, at least from Madam Fauveau and from Mr. Ackerman --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau won't be here. I mean, working on the basis that you're severing. And nor will Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we have discussed this already and I can tell you, the position that we will be taking in this regard, if -- irrespective of what we will decide on -- on the provisional release matter -- is that if you choose to proceed with the trial jointly - I mean the two accused as co-accused - then that will also be our decision. Our decision may change if at some later point in time we see or we come to the conclusion that the trial itself is being obstructed, hampered, or is difficult to proceed with the two accused together. So we will not at this point in time take a decision to sever the two accused unless we have a specific request coming from you or even maybe from the Defence. I mean, we would -- we would entertain a motion from the Defence too in that regard. But we will not be taking a decision ourselves at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, Your Honour, I'm very grateful for that indication, and I will -- I would like to be heard, then -- in fact, if Your Honours would care to rise, I'm going take instructions straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if we -- if you let us know, then obviously we can plan ahead better.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think in that case, can I ask Your Honours to rise for 15 minutes, because I do think that we need to -- before Your Honours leave now. And Your Honours are going to issue a written decision, as I understand it, on the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will. And may I also assure everyone that the fact that we are handing down a written decision will not in any way delay our decision unduly. It will delay it by a little bit necessarily, because it's something that has to be drafted and checked and re-checked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, so I see Mr. Ackerman wants to say something, Your Honour. So before I carry on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first thing I will tell you is that -- that I will object very strongly to this case going forward as a joint trial with General Talic not being here. And there are many reasons for that. There -- the main one is that his counsel will not no longer be able to take instructions from him in any kind of a meaningful way and so it will just almost become a sham trial where we're pretending like someone is on trial and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why are you saying what they will be unable to do before we actually hear what they will be able or unable to do? Because at least --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm just making an assumption, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because at least Mr. Zecevic has already informed us that he should be in a position on a weekly basis to tell us, given the names of the witnesses -- so I presume that he assumes and he presumes that he will be in continuous contact with his client.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I -- I seriously doubt that if your client is not in The Hague that you will have anywhere near the kind of contact with that client that you would have when your client is here. You have daily contact here. You go to the detention centre with some frequency to discuss matters. That's not likely to happen. But I want to leave that aside at this point. I will object to a joint trial with General Talic not being here. I will file a motion to sever these cases and go forward with the Brdjanin case separate from the Talic case. And I can file that as quickly, I suppose, as tomorrow if Your Honours would like me to. But I strongly object to going forward as a joint trial with General Talic not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. As we have already said, with all due respect to Mr. John Ackerman's comment, as we have informed the Trial Chamber, we are very well aware of this situation and we have -- we have committed ourselves and our client has committed ourselves to have -- we have as clear instruction for this witness and the next two witnesses, and what I have said -- we are -- we are standing on the same point that we will inform the Trial Chamber each Thursday about the next -- the next coming week. And we believe that we can have enough instruction that we need for -- from our client. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do need to add, so there's no misunderstanding, that I'm perfectly willing to sit next week and finish up with Mr. Filipovic in the context of a joint trial. And if there's time, even take the next witness. But after that, I would be concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And to think of it, that it was General Talic who in the first place asked for his case to be heard and dealt with separately from that of Brdjanin. Yes. Anyway, I think we'll rise for 15 minutes. I think it will be helpful for us to know exactly what the position which will -- the Prosecution prefers at the present moment will be. And then we'll act accordingly. It could also be a combination of both, along the lines that Mr. Ackerman has suggested. I don't know. But for the present moment, our message to you is that we will proceed with a joint -- a joint trial unless the situation asks for a change and a separation of the two accused, or the two trials. That's the position.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, do I understand it that if effectively -- amazingly enough Mr. Ackerman and I agree on something, Your Honours will then act as -- as we require?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can take it at that. Unless -- because we -- we, like you, do have the interest of -- we have an interest that this case goes on. That's the -- our responsibility as a Trial Chamber is to ensure that this case goes on. Now, whether it goes on against the two accused together or the two accused separately depends very much first on your preferences, secondly on the events as they develop. There may come a situation whereby today we may decide that it's in the better interest -- the best interests of justice to proceed with the two cases jointly, and tomorrow the situation may change. I mean, General Talic may start, for example, on -- chemotherapy and we end up with a week --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Quite. Your Honours just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Your Honours just hit the nail on the head. If -- and I have to say that that's what my instructions are at the moment if Your Honours are prepared to comply with it. But if it goes on against both, the stop-start aspect of this trial, not to mention the cost of getting witnesses up who sit on days for end not doing anything, is just horrifying to contemplate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But that's your responsibility, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour is quite right. It is my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the reason why we are saying tell us your preference and then we will act accordingly is precisely because we don't want to take on our shoulders the responsibility which is strictly yours at this point in time. You realise as much as we do that irrespective of where General Talic will be in the next weeks, he may well be in a position where, having told us, "I waive my right to be present for the proceedings," may not be even worth the paper it's written on. So please do take everything into consideration, come back with a -- your preference, and you can rest assured that we will not be insensitive to the needs, both of the Prosecution and of the two Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. My instructions were that the Trial Chamber should rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours have now thrown it back to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So I will make sure that we arrive at a decision within 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Whoever gave you those instructions should realise that this is not the first time that we are -- at least, I myself, dealing with a situation like this. Okay. Fifteen minutes, or as long as you require.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will be in our chambers and you just let us know when you want us to resume. Okay, 15 minutes. --- Break taken at 3.19 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very grateful for the time that Your Honours allowed me. Your Honours, I have the conduct of this case, and I have to use my professional judgement in deciding what is the proper method to proceed when an accused person is too ill to be physically present for his trial where the continuance of his trial depends on two things: First, his continued waiver, whether given on a weekly or a daily basis; second, his ability to give instructions to his counsel as to the witnesses or as to the nature of the evidence to be given by witnesses who will be forthcoming. We also have a duty as an office, it is my professional judgement, to consider the prospect of witnesses coming to court to give evidence on matters which are of a deeply emotional and emotive nature and being told that they cannot give that evidence because one of the accused is not in a position to give instructions. And having heard what Mr. Ackerman on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin has to say, that he will in any event be applying for Your Honours to sever the trial, Your Honours, it is my considered professional judgement that we cannot proceed with General Talic being absent and the trial against him going on. It will be our application, I hope, at some stage, if things progress more optimistically than as at present stated, that there will come a trial -- I'm sorry, there will come a time when there is a trial of General Talic, but this cannot be at present, and therefore our application is that Your Honours sever the case against General Talic as of today or tomorrow, whenever you make your ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We have -- Your Honours, we have clearly stated our position. We don't think that the severance of the case is needed at this time. I have explained to Ms. Korner that this is just a technical matter, whether we would get the information on Tuesday or Thursday. If we get the information on Tuesday, we can inform the Trial Chamber and the Prosecutor about the waiver of our client for the coming week, so it will have much -- more than enough time to inform the witnesses and all that. As to the severance of the case, we leave that in the hands of the Trial Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, I suppose you have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So at this point I think I can assure you that early tomorrow morning or early in the day tomorrow morning we should be in a position to hand down both decisions as regards the severance of the two accused and as well as on the motion for provisional release and response -- Prosecutor's response.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just add, then, I've spoken to Mr. Ackerman and I imagine the same would apply in any event, depending on Your Honours' decision to the counsel for General Talic. We will attempt to get Mr. Filipovic back next week. It may not be Monday now, because of the difficulties of arranging flights and giving him adequate warning. I was reminded that the court in any event is not sitting next Friday either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's -- basically what I suggest we do -- let me hear what Madam Fauveau has to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then we'll deal with everything. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have just heard Madam Korner say a couple of minutes ago that my client is not physically capable of attending the proceedings, and in fact Ms. Korner is right. But what I wish to tell this Chamber is that when Ms. Korner says that General Talic is not capable of attending when that suits her and when we request provisional release, then she says that he is capable. But I must say that in this case, Ms. Korner is right; he is not capable of attending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think what we have to decide upon is this: Number one, the two decisions that will be handed down tomorrow, to start with, followed by a decision as -- which depends on you -- as to whether to bring Mr. Filipovic over next week to continue his evidence -- cross-examination, Mr. Ackerman. And if that is possible, I would suggest that you communicate with Mr. Ackerman to make all the necessary arrangements. We are at your disposal the whole of next week except Friday, if I remember well, because that was the understanding. However, if it needs be, if needs be, unless you have commitments and we need to sit Friday, we will sit Friday. So that is -- I'm making this quite -- quite clear. But I don't think the cross-examination is anticipated to go beyond -- beyond Thursday. That's number one. Number two: I don't know, given what Mr. Ackerman hinted at the last time we sat -- I don't know if in continuing and concluding his examination he requires some kind of assistance from the two counsel for General Talic. I would reserve your position on that. I don't know what your preference is, and I would like to hear what -- what you have to say in this regard, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I probably didn't make myself as clear earlier as I should have. But what I was suggesting is that even if there is to be a severance in this case that it not happen until we finish the cross-examination of Mr. Filipovic for this simple reason: Mr. -- Mr. Zecevic is prepared to conduct a significant portion of that cross-examination; I'm not. I'd prefer that he do it rather than take the time to prepare that portion of the cross myself. And so if it was -- if the Chamber decided that severance was the proper result, that that order be effective after the testimony of Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you concur with that, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We concur, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I take it that we will also have the consent of General Talic to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As I already informed the Trial Chamber, we have the consent of General Talic for this witness and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But after having heard, Madam Fauveau, I want to make sure that he is in a condition to proceed with that waiver.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that waiver was given last Tuesday. So we informed the Trial Chamber at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So would you agree, Ms. Korner, that we postpone the decision on the severance until Mr. Filipovic has concluded his evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it's a device, Your Honour, but I'm not going to raise any particular objection to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So -- okay. That's agreed. That's agreed. After that, there will be a decision taken. We could actually take the decision, making it effective after the -- we could do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's one other matter - I'm sorry - which arose out of the matter that I raised with you last week, and that's the question of the article that was published. There was apparently some query from the Defence as to whether the translation was accurate in mentioning closed session. So we've had it properly -- I say properly. We've had a rough translation. This is an authorised CLSS translation so that Your Honours can see it. We can hand that in to Your Honours after court and to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The only question is when Your Honours intended to deal with that. It may be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, as soon as we have an indication of the person that is responsible that could be summoned to appear before us, we could do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I understood that the Registry was going to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't been informed as yet, at least. I haven't received information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I think Your Honour did inquire of the Registry whether they could achieve that. I think we can probably through our own press some people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. I said that this article was badly quoted during the last hearing. In this article, the word "closed session" doesn't appear anywhere, and those words do not appear in the article, and it seems that those word bothered Ms. Korner the most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that the authorised translation -- perhaps I can hand it in now and give the Defence a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do I take it -- I mean, I don't know enough about the background, but is this a -- an Internet newspaper?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or sit an ordinary newspaper? What is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think it's an ordinary -- I think it's an ordinary newspaper. And like many others, the articles, then, are recycled for the -- but I wouldn't swear to that. As I say, it's not a publication I've come across before. If you look at the first few lines, it states that "Momir Talic, the Bosnian Serb army general indicted for genocide by the Tribunal in The Hague is going home, or rather, to hospital. Following several days of hearings closed to the public --" and then it gives the content of what was said during those days of hearings closed to the public, and fairly accurately too. And then in paragraph 2 begins: "According to Dani's information at the hearing Wednesday, which was in closed session, discussions were held about what to do next." So I'm not quite clear what Madam Fauveau means when she says there's no reference to closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no reference that something said in this article comes from a closed-session hearing. However, that is what Ms. Korner said at the previous sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- we won't cross this at this moment. What I would require to know is the person responsible -- some further information on this, the person responsible for this publication. I see -- I notice that the website is -- refers to BH Dani. It could be the name of this person himself. I don't know. But please check and when we have enough information, we can come back to you and tell you the way we're going proceed and when.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I think it won't take very long for us to provide you the name of the author.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. It shouldn't be difficult because I see this is a properly registered -- and it has also got copyright. So I would imagine that you should be able to trace -- if there is a press register, which I would imagine there is. Any further -- so I take it that next week we will be working -- proceeding with the cross-examination of Mr. Filipovic. Do I take it that that will be all for next week?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it depends when we can get him here. I'm unanxious to bring up another witness from Bosnia because of having to send them back if we don't finish. But I'm going to make inquiries today and tomorrow as to what can be achieved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then after that I imagine that you still require some time to reorganise --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, we'll use the week that we're not sitting to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's perfect. Is that okay with you, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, there's a great -- there's a number of imponderables that I think will have to await your decision tomorrow before I can begin to pursue them and then I can communicate with you all as to where I think we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair enough. I thank you. We'll now rise. I am informed that the translation of the communication of the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia should be ready by now, and the official translation should be ready in an hour's time. I thank you. We will be working on it -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tomorrow, yes, of course. Tomorrow we will be handing down the decisions. And I am going to hand the decisions in open session. So we will communicate to you the time. It will probably be sometime in the morning -- in the second half of the morning, the second half of the morning, hoping that we finish by then. All right? Thank you.
